clue.text: Type of billiards peculiar to Powys?

definitions.text: Type of billiards peculiar to Powys?

parts.words: Type of billiards peculiar to Powys?
parts.note: a cue game of pockets and balls played the way they do it in Wales, read also as the name of a market town in that Welsh county

explanation.surface: A question about some regional variant of billiards played in a Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: Powys is a county in mid-Wales; its town of Welshpool splits into WELSH POOL, a pool game from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The town's name divides into a Welsh form of the cue game pool, and the town lies in that county.

clue.text: One German right in Ireland

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside the other piece here

parts.note: ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A German man claims some legal right while living in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is a poetic name for the island and nation of Ireland.

clue.text: Help to sample the wine

parts.note: to sup is to take a small taste or sip of a drink
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Encouragement to go and taste the wine on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or assist someone is to help them, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fruitful Greek. god previously a cat, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: previously gives PRIOR and a cat is a PUSS, together sounding like the name of the god

explanation.surface: A fertile Greek deity who, in some earlier life, was reportedly a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray full stop after 'Greek' is a printing slip. Said aloud, PRIOR PUSS sounds like the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Priapus was the Greek fertility deity of gardens and livestock, hence fruitful.

clue.text: Sort out bits and pieces

indicators.note: out here suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up a heap of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SORT to ORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps or leftovers, especially of food, so odd fragments.

clue.text: Skill well displayed with the quince

parts.note: well as an adjective means good, fine or satisfactory

indicators.note: displayed hints that the letters are spread out and laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shows a deft touch when handling the fruit called a quince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' as an adjective is GOOD; 'displayed' tells you to lay the letters of 'the quince' out in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound method of doing something is expertise or skill.

clue.text: Secret agent sheltering from the rain?

explanation.surface: A spy who is also keeping dry in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy working in disguise is an undercover operative, and a person beneath a roof or umbrella is literally beneath cover.

clue.text: Evidently not as pretty as a picture

definitions.text: Evidently not as pretty as a picture

parts.words: Evidently not as pretty as a picture
parts.note: a jokey phrase for a plain-looking person, read literally as not being a canvas of artwork

explanation.surface: A remark that someone plainly falls short of being lovely to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appears without its letter count in the print; the answer is (2,3,8).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone unattractive by saying they are no artwork, a stock expression for plain looks.

clue.text: Units making no secret about the pound

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters are placed around another piece
making signals that the following letters are worked into something new, an anagram

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Some people are quite open about how much money they earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges NO SECRET into E-ECTRONS, and 'about' puts it around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrons are elementary particles, the basic unit of negative electric charge.

clue.text: Part of San Francisco to be found in the Potteries?

definitions.text: to be found in the Potteries?

explanation.surface: Asking where a district of San Francisco might be found in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries is the area round Stoke-on-Trent in England, famous for making china, so any town there is a china town.
explanation.definitionFit: San Francisco has a famous Chinese quarter, and a pottery town in Staffordshire is a town of porcelain.

clue.text: Game played at the end of a Honolulu party

indicators.note: at the end of here picks the closing letters of Honolulu, its last two

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or social event

explanation.surface: A board game played to finish off a celebration in Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'at the end of' takes the final pair LU of Honolulu, not just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game of dice and counters, so it is a type of game.

clue.text: Car to manage round a bend

indicators.note: round signals that one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to cope is to manage or get by
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: A driver trying to handle a vehicle going around a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts COPE around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupe is a two-door motor vehicle with a fixed roof.

clue.text: Net result of disentangling hems

indicators.note: disentangling suggests untangling and rearranging the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: The final outcome of unpicking the edges of some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net result' reads as a final outcome, but 'Net' is the definition and 'result of' a link; 'disentangling' rearranges HEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is a woven fabric with open spaces, like a net.

clue.text: Operatic heroine takes on northern saint

indicators.note: takes on means one piece adds the next onto its end

parts.note: Aida is the title heroine of Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: A singer of opera adopts the role of a holy figure from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: St Aidan was the monk who founded Lindisfarne in Northumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidan of Lindisfarne is a canonised holy man of the early English church.

clue.text: Position in the factory

explanation.surface: Someone's job title or place within a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something firmly is to position it, and an industrial works is a manufacturing site.

clue.text: Border uprisings ruffle this evil loch

indicators.note: to ruffle is to disturb or disorder, signalling a rearrangement of letters

explanation.surface: Rebellions on a frontier disturb a sinister Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprisings' looks like rebellions but means ground rising, hills; 'ruffle' rearranges THIS EVIL LOCH. The range runs along the England-Scotland border.
explanation.definitionFit: The range forms part of the boundary between England and Scotland, so its heights rise on the frontier.

clue.text: Elementary to say it goes with chips

definitions.text: Elementary to say it goes with chips

parts.words: Elementary to say it goes with chips
parts.note: a chemical element that pairs with chips in computing, not with fish or fries

explanation.surface: Plainly stating what accompanies a plate of fries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary' means it is a chemical element; the chips are microchips, not fries.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiconducting chemical element used for computer microchips.

clue.text: Makes Theresa warm again

definitions.note: the definition is the bare verb; the answer is its third-person form

indicators.note: makes here means the letters are built up into a new word

explanation.surface: Theresa gets something heated up once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' rearranges THERESA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To heat cooked food a second time is to warm it once more.

clue.text: Do as a confidence trickster does

definitions.text: Do as a confidence trickster does

parts.words: Do as a confidence trickster does
parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, the work of a con artist

explanation.definitionFit: To con or cheat someone out of money is to defraud them, the trickster's trade.

clue.text: Asian bird attended by a small animal doctor

indicators.note: attended by means the first piece is accompanied by the next one following

parts.note: mini means small
a vet is a veterinary surgeon who treats animals

explanation.surface: A bird from Asia brought to a veterinary surgeon of short stature.
explanation.definitionFit: The minivet is a brightly coloured songbird of southern and eastern Asia.

clue.text: Most gentle headmaster with the idlest form

parts.note: the head of master is its first letter M

indicators.note: form suggests the letters are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A kindly school head teaches the laziest class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headmaster' looks like a school head but means the head of 'master'; 'form' is a school class in the surface and the anagram signal in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of mild, meaning gentlest or softest.

clue.text: Kinnock steps out of line

indicators.note: steps out of suggests a word breaking ranks, so its letters move out of order

explanation.surface: A politician breaks ranks with the party.
explanation.walkthrough: Neil Kinnock led the UK Labour Party in the 1980s; 'steps out of' rearranges LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Kinnock is a former British Labour leader, so Kinnock's first name.

clue.text: See 16
Pull backward

indicators.note: back, the first half of the clue's last word, says to read the other half from end to start

parts.note: taken as written, the second half of the word backward; that the whole word read in reverse also shows the answer is a coincidence of this split, not a separate hidden word

explanation.surface: An instruction to tug something towards you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' splits into 'back' and 'ward': WARD turned back gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a cart or curtain is to drag or tug it.

clue.text: Not half uncommon in Scotland

indicators.note: half here takes the first four of the word's eight letters

explanation.surface: A remark that something is pretty unusual north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very'; in Scots the answer means both 'very' and 'strange'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word means remarkably or strange, so very unusual in Scottish speech.

clue.text: The point is what you used to be

parts.note: E, for east, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone tells you the crux is who you once were.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the old form of 'you', so it is what 'you' used to be.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic object form of the second person singular was replaced by the modern word.

clue.text: Looked back on the way success spoiled the girl

explanation.surface: A girl glanced over her shoulder while fame went to her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned her head' means both glanced behind her and, of success, made her vain.
explanation.definitionFit: Glancing behind means twisting the face round, and fame that makes someone conceited is said to go to their head.

clue.text: Do they include a new line in neckwear?

definitions.text: Do they include a new line in neckwear?

parts.words: Do they include a new line in neckwear?
parts.note: new items generally, read also as fresh fashion cravats, new-style neckties

explanation.surface: A question about whether a range of gimmicky gifts features some fresh ties.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOVEL TIES, the answer is new neckties.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelties are new or unusual items, and novel ties would be a new line in neckwear.
